描述_ZN: Scroll of Reading Paintings, modern, painted by Chen Shizeng, on paper with color, 87.7 cm long and 46.6 cm wide.　　Self-titled: "December 1, Dingsi, Ye Yufu, Jin Gongbei, Chen Zhongyu, all of the capital collectors in the Central Park exhibition for seven days, changing daily, a total of 600 to 700 kinds, to take the viewer's fee to the capital of the floods, because the picture of its time to remember the event." 　　The self-titled "Dingsi" for the sixth year of the Republic of China (1917).　　The creation of this figure is based on real historical events, in 1917, the domestic floods, a group of prominent people in the cultural and artistic circles in Beijing to carry out voluntary acts, in Central Park, now Beijing Zhongshan Park exhibition to raise funds for disaster relief. The exhibition brought together six or seven hundred works, a considerable scale. The three people mentioned in the self-titled exhibition were all leading figures in Beijing's literary and artistic circles at the time.　　The painter was present at the exhibition and recorded the scenes he saw from the perspective of his first vision, which was realistic and vivid, close to the realism of news photos. There are young and old Chinese in robes and coats, westerners in western clothes and blondes, and fashionable women in western clothes. The faces of the people in the painting are simple and casual, with some caricature. The author omits lines and directly uses large blocks of ink to shape the figures' forms, with short, thin lines that are only partially outlined, and also uses a technique close to "flying white" to represent the brighter parts of the objects' lighted surfaces. This omission of lines and the perception and expression of light are very different from traditional Chinese painting techniques, which shows Chen Shizeng's Western painting attainments.　　With its traditional proposition, fresh content, and a combination of Chinese and Western techniques, "Reading Paintings" is a reflection of Chen Shizeng's creative painting practice and exploration.
